title: Olympus M.Zuiko Digital 45 mm F1.8 Lens $245.19 Delivered @ Amazon Japan via AU
body:
Deal: Olympus M.Zuiko Digital 45 mm F1.8 Lens $245.19 Delivered @ Amazon Japan via AU

[stimutacs] Yup if you are shooting photos of people or places - and it doesn't need to be wide angle or a big group of people from close distance - this is an absolute no brainer thing to own if you have any m43 camera at all.
[kingarthur] I’ve been using this lens for years. Not the sharpest but quite fun lens and definitely worth it for a compact portrait lens on a budget.
[lawyerz] one of my favourite lenses when I was still shooting with m43
[kingarthur] I cannot let M43 go. It's so lovely that I sometimes prefer using it over my full frame Sony.
[lawyerz] I still have my m43 too, sentimental value and took some of my favourite pics of all time.
I wish they continued development on the bodies and continued focusing on small form factor instead of pivoting to wildlife photography with large lenses
[Thayer] The M43 system is so good for sport and wildlife. Having had FF Lumix, Sony, & Canon, I cannot match MFT for anywhere near the size, price and performance.
It helps that run out models have deep discounts and ~$1,500 lenses can be found secondhand for ~$400.
The vintage glow of the Voigtlander 17.5mm & 42.5mm f/0.95, to the 3D pop of the Olympus 75mm f/1.8, nearly all my favourite photos are from MFT.
[lawyerz] @Thayer: 75mm F1.8 was the GOAT. Even now I miss it so much
[stimutacs] @Thayer: I would need something that did around 78mp at 60fps in an FF sensor to consider switching off m43. I've tried it last year with some fairly pricey FF gear, there is no equivalent long macro lens that gives anything like the quality/range/weight/speed I get from the system, and nothing weatherproof all down the line either.
[Thayer] Tack sharp wide open with high micro-contrast and a smooth fall-off.
Nothing comes close to the price-to-performance ratio until the 75mm f/1.8.
[BROKENKEYBOARD] also in black for $1 more https://www.amazon.com.au/Olympus-Zuiko-Digital-Panasonic-Ca…
[Rumboocha] if you had to pick 1, would you pick this or a 25mm lens?
[stimutacs] It's going to be a personal choice but I do most of my native lens shooting these days on the lumix 9mm f1.7 and the oly 60mm 2.8 (and longer adapted lenses). The 2x crop 15-30mm range is the kind of thing most phone cameras do very well and I'd struggle to find a thing I'd pull out the camera for instead of a phone.
[NoobStyles] If you're doing portraits this. Otherwise if you can only have 1 I'd pick the 25mm because wider is more versatile
[Jimothy Wongingtons] I have both oly 25 1.8 and the 45 , I vote 25 personally
[Thayer] ~25mm lens is a versatile EDC for almost all genres of photography & videography.
The 45mm for portraits and special occasions generally, but not limited to.
[Rumboocha] current lenses are:
Olympus M.Zuiko Digital ED 12mm f/2.0
Olympus M.Zuiko Digital ED 14–42mm f/3.5–5.6 EZ Pancake
Olympus M.Zuiko Digital ED 40–150mm f/4–5.6 R
so would only pick between this or the 25mm
[Munki] Very different lenses… What do you shoot most?
[Rumboocha] at the moment mostly the zoom lens. kids sports etc.
Travel to japan was mostly on the 12mm
[Thayer] The 45mm f/1.8 will offer the biggest impact and lvl up SOOC.
[squaredonut] If I could add another option, it would be the 75mm f1.8, I really miss that lens, but I don't even have a m4/3 camera anymore, but the 75mm was such a nice portrait, especially for its size compared to all the other systems equivalent one.
[takemymoney] This is 10year old pricing…if only I still used my m43 which is stored somewhere…
[Mugsy] I was just thinking the same thing… "if only I still used my m43".
I actually took my E-M10 mk2 down to Tasmania earlier this year. Lugged it around Dove Lake even. I mainly used my S23 Ultra to take photos… I even forgot how to input the settings I wanted on the camera. That's what 6-7yrs of not using it will do.
This lens would be great for portraits though. But the phone gets the portrait photos my wife wants with less hassle. Wife would get frustrated as I relearn to take a good photo manually.
[takemymoney] Same - I don't even know how to setup anymore I guess. I think it has been 6 years since I didn't touch my m43…now that I'm thinking, time to inspect the battery….
[Thayer] The standard "pro" configuration for street and portrait photographers who want the speed of a point-and-shoot:
Mode 'A' (Aperture Priority)
S-AF (Single AF)
Single Centre Point
AF-S + MF
Simply set them once, and the camera is ready to shoot immediately.
[adrianhughes1998] Miss my old 45 1.8, can absolutely vouch for this lens. With eye autofocus you can nail tack sharp images, even when zoomed in
[Zackeroo] My dad gave me his old GH5 with this 45mm 1.8, 25mm 1.7 and a 14-140.
The 45 is my favourite lens of the lot by far. Excellent lens, surprised to see it here.
